newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill four in Karachi ambush.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill four in Karachi ambush.

text.p: Gunmen killed two sons of a senior police official along with their driver and a guard in an ambush on Friday in the southern city of Karachi, police said.
They said Kashif Aziz and his brother Rashid Aziz, sons of deputy superindendent of police Azizur Rehman, were killed when four gunmen opened fire on their car outside a mosque.
Witnesses said the victims, after attending Friday Moslem prayers, were sitting in their car outside the mosque apparently preparing to leave for home when the gunmen in another car shot them.
All four victims died on the spot and police said the gunmen escaped.
They said Kashif Aziz was himself a sub-inspector in the police Federal Investigation Agency, while the driver and the guard were police constables.
Azizur Rehman, talking to reporters at the hospital where the bodies were taken, accused militants of the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) of carrying out the ambush.
An MQM spokesman denied any involvement.
There has been a renewed surge in political violence in Karachi, where dozens of people have died in the past few weeks in attacks involving rival MQM factions.
Police say more than 160 people have been killed in Karachi's political violence since March 1 compared to 500 in 1996 and more than 2,000 in 1995.
The MQM speaks for Urdu-speaking people who migrated from India at Partition in 1947 and their descendants.
